title: Watchlist: animated skeleton row while a newly-added ticker's data is still loading
description:
User request: adding a ticker to the watchlist should immediately show an animated skeleton placeholder, since it can take a moment before the ticker actually appears with real data -- so the user gets visual feedback that something is happening rather than the UI looking unresponsive.

Current behavior: AddTickerForm.tsx's submit button already shows a loading spinner while POST /api/watchlist itself is in flight, but POST just adds the ticker row (fast) -- useAddWatchlistItem.ts's onSuccess invalidates the whole watchlist query, triggering a GET /api/watchlist refetch that computes a signal for EVERY watched ticker (including the brand-new one, whose signal has never been computed/cached before) -- this refetch, not the POST, is the actual source of the perceptible delay before the new ticker's real row (with its ticker/date/signal/confidence) appears in WatchlistTable.tsx. The button's own spinner clears once the POST resolves, before the slower part is even done, which is exactly the gap the user is describing.

Use MUI's Skeleton component for the animated placeholder -- this is a genuinely new pattern in this codebase (the existing common/LoadingState is a whole-page spinner, not a per-row/inline skeleton), so this task introduces the first one; decide whether it's worth generalizing into a reusable common/ component now or is fine as a one-off in WatchlistTable for this single use case, and record as a decisions entry.

checklist.step: Decide where 'which ticker is currently being added' state lives so both AddTickerForm (which owns the mutation) and WatchlistTable (which renders the row) can see it -- e.g. lift to WatchlistPage, or another mechanism -- and when exactly the skeleton appears/disappears (on submit vs. on POST success; disappears once the ticker's real row is present in the refetched list, or on error). Record as a decisions entry.
Implement an animated skeleton row in WatchlistTable.tsx for the pending ticker, using MUI's Skeleton component.
Handle the error case: if POST fails, remove the skeleton and surface it via the existing ErrorState path in AddTickerForm rather than leaving an orphaned skeleton row.

Handle the already-watched/idempotent-no-op case (POST/API.md) sensibly -- the row already exists, so the skeleton either doesn't apply or resolves immediately, not a lingering placeholder for a row that was already there.

Tests: submitting a valid new ticker shows the skeleton then the real row; a failing add clears the skeleton and shows the error; a duplicate add doesn't leave a stray skeleton (MSW-mocked, including a deliberately delayed mock response to actually exercise the in-between skeleton state).
Confirm 90% coverage gate still holds, Storybook covers the new skeleton state if it became its own common/ component, and run make e2e to confirm nothing broke on the watchlist add flow.

decisions.decision: The 'which ticker is currently being added' state that both AddTickerForm and WatchlistTable need is read directly off useAddWatchlistItem's shared TanStack Query mutation-cache entry, via `useMutationState({ filters: { mutationKey: watchlistKeys.add, status: 'pending' } })` inside WatchlistTable -- not lifted into a common ancestor (WatchlistPage) and prop-drilled down to both children. The skeleton appears the instant `mutate()` dispatches (on submit) and persists through both the POST and the GET refetch it triggers, because useAddWatchlistItem.ts's `onSuccess` now *awaits* `queryClient.invalidateQueries` instead of firing it off. It disappears on error (mutation status flips to 'error', excluded by the 'pending' filter) or once the refetch completes and the real row is present in `items` (checked every WatchlistTable render).
decisions.rationale: AddTickerForm and WatchlistTable are siblings under WatchlistPage with no other state they need to share, and useMutationState is a native TanStack Query mechanism for exactly this (observing a mutation's state from anywhere, keyed by `mutationKey`), keeping the app within 'TanStack Query only' (Frontend.md §2) without introducing prop-drilling or a new Context. Awaiting invalidateQueries in onSuccess keeps the mutation's `status` at 'pending' (matching the useMutationState filter) for the entire window during which the new ticker's real data isn't yet visible -- exactly the gap the task describes -- and as a side effect keeps AddTickerForm's own submit button loading/disabled for that same whole window instead of appearing to finish early. Rejected alternative: lifting the `useAddWatchlistItem()` call itself into WatchlistPage and passing the resulting mutation object down as a prop to both AddTickerForm and WatchlistTable -- rejected because it would force AddTickerForm's public API and its existing standalone tests to change for a concern that is purely about cross-component *visibility*, not mutation *ownership*, which useMutationState already solves without that restructuring.

decisions.decision: MUI's Skeleton is used directly inline in WatchlistTable's per-column `render` callbacks as a one-off, not generalized into a new components/common/ wrapper despite being the first per-row/inline skeleton pattern in this codebase.
decisions.rationale: Every existing common/ component (SignalBadge, ConfidenceGauge, LoadingState, ErrorState, ...) encapsulates real domain- or convention-specific behavior (coloring rules, band thresholds, a message layout) beyond what the underlying MUI primitive already provides. There is exactly one usage site here (WatchlistTable's own columns) and no shared prop surface or behavior to abstract -- each cell just needs a differently-sized MUI Skeleton with no domain logic attached, the same way AddTickerForm already uses raw MUI Button/TextField directly without a common/ wrapper. Revisit this if a second per-row skeleton use case appears elsewhere (e.g. PositionsTable) and the two genuinely need to share behavior, not just both happen to render MUI's Skeleton.

decisions.decision: The already-watched/idempotent-no-op add case is handled by simply never adding a synthetic skeleton row for a ticker that's already present in the current `items` list at render time -- i.e. 'the skeleton doesn't apply', the first of the two options the checklist itself allows, rather than 'resolves immediately'.
decisions.rationale: A real row for that ticker is already visible on screen the instant the (idempotent) POST is submitted, so there is nothing to placeholder and nothing to explicitly resolve -- checking `items.some(item => item.ticker === pendingTicker)` against the already-fetched list (not any newly introduced state) is sufficient and avoids ever rendering a duplicate/ghost row alongside the real one.

comments.summary: Non-blocking: the synthetic pending-add row's `added_at: ''` isn't treated as 'missing' by DataTable's sort comparator (which only special-cases null/undefined), so sorting the 'Added' column ascending puts the skeleton row at the top instead of a stable position, and it visibly jumps to the bottom the instant the real (newest-timestamped) row replaces it -- mirror-image issue when sorted descending. Tracked as frontend-watchlist-add-skeleton-followups.

Non-blocking: the WatchlistRow doc comment claims 'every column's render below swaps in an animated MUI Skeleton for this row', but the action column (confidence_band key) correctly renders null instead for a pending row (no remove action makes sense for a not-yet-real row) -- the comment overstates actual behavior. Tracked as frontend-watchlist-add-skeleton-followups.

review.notes: Full review of PR #132. Backend unchanged (no diff under backend/, no OpenAPI check applicable). Coverage: backend pytest --cov 99.86% (573 passed, gate untouched since no backend changes), frontend vitest --coverage 99.69% statements / 99.44% branches (343 passed) -- both well above the 90% gate. Static analysis clean on both sides: backend ruff + mypy (no issues), frontend eslint + tsc -b --noEmit (no issues). code-review skill (medium effort) ran and returned exactly the two non-blocking findings recorded above (sort-order sentinel, doc-comment overstatement) -- no correctness bugs, no reuse/efficiency issues. No new module/dependency/layer introduced (useMutationState is an existing export of the already-installed @tanstack/react-query, confirmed against node_modules), so architecture-review wasn't separately invoked. No new component file added under components/common/ or a features/ folder -- the Skeleton usage is inline in the existing WatchlistTable.tsx per this task's own recorded (and reasonable) decision not to promote it, so the 7a placement question doesn't newly arise here. area is frontend/pages/watchlist, not backend/signals or backend/portfolio, so verify-elder-signal doesn't apply. Ran make e2e: 16/16 specs passed, including the pre-existing watchlist.spec.ts golden path (add/remove with a real fixture-backed signal) -- no regression. Did a live browser walkthrough (yarn dev + fixture-mode uvicorn manually started; no Playwright MCP tool registered in this session, so drove real Chromium directly via playwright-core from a scratch script instead, screenshots taken) covering all three scenarios the task calls for: (1) added a brand-new ticker (MSFT) with the GET refetch triggered by invalidateQueries deliberately delayed via page.route -- the animated skeleton row appeared immediately on submit across all 4 data columns, the Add button stayed disabled/loading for the whole window, no real MSFT row was visible while the skeleton showed, and the skeleton cleanly resolved into the real row (HOLD/confidence gauge) the instant the delayed GET resolved, not after any fixed timer; (2) re-added an already-watched ticker (AAPL) -- confirmed zero skeleton cells ever rendered and no duplicate row appeared; (3) forced the POST to fail (mocked 500) for a not-yet-watched ticker (GOOGL) -- confirmed the skeleton never persisted/orphaned, the ErrorState alert appeared with the failure detail, and no stray GOOGL row was added. No console errors or failed-request entries beyond the deliberately-triggered 500 itself. Verified via node_modules/@tanstack/query-core source that useMutationState's mutationKey filter does a partial (prefix) match by default, so `watchlistKeys.add` correctly scopes to exactly this mutation and no other; verified AddTickerForm's MUI Button `loading` prop disables the button, so only one add can be in flight at a time in the real UI, matching this task's own documented rationale for using `.at(-1)` on the pending-mutations array. Unit and integration tests (WatchlistTable.test.tsx, WatchlistPage.test.tsx) genuinely exercise the delayed-response skeleton-then-real-row, error-clears-skeleton, and duplicate-add-no-stray-skeleton cases (not just asserted without a real async gap), matching what the browser walkthrough independently confirmed. All checklist items phrased as 'decide X' have corresponding decisions entries with real rationale (pending-state location via useMutationState, one-off vs common/ Skeleton, idempotent-duplicate no-skeleton handling); no undocumented judgment calls found. Two non-blocking findings recorded above and filed as frontend-watchlist-add-skeleton-followups.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran backend pytest --cov (573 passed, 99.86%) and frontend vitest --coverage (343 passed, 99.69%/99.44%) -- both match pr-reviewer's reported numbers exactly. Ran make e2e (16/16 passed) and eslint/tsc (clean). Skimmed the full diff myself (useAddWatchlistItem.ts, queryKeys.ts, AddTickerForm.tsx, WatchlistTable.tsx, both test files) -- matches the review's description; the two non-blocking findings (added_at sort sentinel, WatchlistRow doc-comment overstatement) are correctly filed as frontend-watchlist-add-skeleton-followups (state planned, mirrored in index.json) and are genuinely non-blocking. Additionally drove the add-ticker flow myself with a real Chromium browser via a scratch Playwright spec against the actual e2e webServer stack, deliberately delaying GET /api/watchlist via page.route: confirmed the skeleton row appears immediately on submit, the Add button stays disabled through the held refetch, no real row exists while pending, and the skeleton cleanly resolves into the real AMZN row once the delayed GET completes -- independently reproducing (not just trusting) the timing claim pr-reviewer's own walkthrough made. Scratch spec deleted after the run; no diff left behind.
